Carpenter's square finds a circle's diameter.

Goal: I can prove an angle inscribed in a semicircle is right and opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Corollary: an angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle (its arc is 180 degrees). Theorem: the opposite angles of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle (a cyclic quadrilateral) are supplementary.

Proof: opposite angles intercept the two arcs between their vertices, which together make the whole circle. So the angles add to (1/2)(360) = 180 degrees.

A carpenter's square placed with its corner on the edge of a round table marks a diameter where its edges cross the rim.
